sentence: This project offers imaging tools for mice and rats so researchers can study tumors and other diseased tissues over time.
This project builds a platform of tools and statistical methods to test and standardize how viral communities in the human body are studied.
This project studies how the prefrontal cortex controls arousal and drinking, and how drinking changes that control.
This project tries to find out whether hepatocytes in humans can build a functional biliary system to treat liver diseases.
This project studies how glutamate receptors assemble, are blocked, and work, using biophysical and biochemical approaches.
This project tries to find out the cellular and molecular causes of inflammatory bowel disease.
This project studies how a protein that switches on genes for cardiac muscle function relates to dilated cardiomyopathy.
This project studies how the environment affects the engraftment of muscle progenitors made from pluripotent stem cells.
This project builds computational models of how cancer cells move between drug resistance states and how drugs affect those moves.
This project studies how aging of the matrix around muscle cells changes the way extracellular vesicles help muscle regenerate.
This project supports research on how to treat and prevent diabetes, obesity, and related disorders.
This project collects and shares MRI brain images to help study Alzheimer's disease and dementia.
This project mines bacterial genomes to find natural product structures and enzyme chemistry, and engineers the pathways that make them.
This project tries to find out where viral pathogens spread between people and animals and how outbreaks can be watched for.
This project builds a drug screening pipeline using engineered cell lines to find drugs that block an immune mediator of inflammatory disease.
This project builds a microarray of glycopeptides and glycoproteins to screen how proteoglycans bind other molecules.
This project tries to find out which metabolic pathways support tumor growth and spread in bladder cancer that carries a particular loss.
This project studies how a herpesvirus moves out of the nucleus, a step needed to make infectious virions.
This project studies small molecules that mimic a receptor to see how they inactivate the envelope glycoprotein of HIV.
This project studies how chromatin remodeling controls the way hematopoietic stem cells turn into different cell types.
